root_cause:
crates/forgeplan-core/src/projection/mod.rs:552 — `render_markdown_with_extras` ends with:

    Ok(format!("---\n{}---\n\n{}\n", yaml, body))

It appends `\n` unconditionally, to a `body` that already ends in a newline.

The other half of the round-trip, crates/forgeplan-core/src/artifact/frontmatter.rs:26 —
`parse_frontmatter` returns:

    content[body_start..].trim_start_matches('\n').to_string()

It trims only LEADING newlines (the `---\n\n` separator). Trailing newlines survive verbatim.

So the round trip is: file body ends with k newlines -> parse gives back k -> render writes
k+1. Strictly +1 per render, unbounded. In render_projection_inner
(crates/forgeplan-core/src/projection/mod.rs:290-300) the non-`force_body` path deliberately
re-uses the file body verbatim (`(file_body.to_string(), preserved)`), which is what makes the
growth compound instead of being reset from the DB copy.

The sibling helper `frontmatter::render_frontmatter` (crates/forgeplan-core/src/artifact/frontmatter.rs:36)
does NOT append the trailing `\n` — `format!("---\n{}---\n\n{}", yaml, body)`. That asymmetry is
why `link::add_link` (crates/forgeplan-core/src/link/mod.rs:59) and `stamp_agent_identity`
(projection/mod.rs:592) are byte-stable while the projection render is not. The correct
behaviour already exists in the codebase; the projection path just doesn't use it.

crates/forgeplan-core/src/projection/mod.rs:1137 in `add_link_with_projection`

    if let Err(e) = render_after_mutation(workspace, store, target).await { ... }

PROB-048 symptom #2 "phantom orphan health signal because only the source side was rendered").
Since links are outgoing-only, the target's rendered frontmatter is byte-identical to what was
already on disk — the target render is intended to be a NO-OP. The trailing newline is therefore
the *only* output of a call that was designed to produce no output at all.

The same defect fires on every mutating command, not just link: activate.rs, deprecate.rs,
link.rs, renew.rs, reopen.rs, supersede.rs all call render_after_mutation.

Contract violated: crates/forgeplan-core/src/projection/mod.rs:38 states
"| Re-render | render_projection, render_after_mutation, sync_before_mutation | Idempotent

suggested_fix:
One-line fix at crates/forgeplan-core/src/projection/mod.rs:552 — normalize to exactly one
terminating newline so the render becomes byte-idempotent:

    // before
    Ok(format!("---\n{}---\n\n{}\n", yaml, body))
    // after
    Ok(format!("---\n{}---\n\n{}\n", yaml, body.trim_end_matches('\n')))

Prefer `trim_end_matches('\n')` over `trim_end()`: the latter would also eat trailing spaces
inside the last content line, which is a behaviour change beyond the defect. POSIX text-file
convention (exactly one terminating newline) makes discarding pre-existing trailing blank lines
the right call, but it should be called out in the changeset since it will collapse the 392
already-accreted files on their next mutation.

Regression test (currently nothing guards this — all projection tests use `.contains()`):

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn render_projection_is_byte_idempotent() {
        // render once, read bytes, render again with identical inputs,
        // assert_eq!(first, second) on raw bytes -- not contains()
    }

Add the same assertion for the target side of `add_link_with_projection`, since that render is
specified to be a no-op for the target and is the path the operator actually hit.

Two follow-ups worth separating from the fix:
1. One-time normalization sweep of the 392 affected files. It touches `.forgeplan/*.md`, so per
   RED LINE #11 it must not be a bare `sed` — either a dedicated `forgeplan fmt`-style command
   or a scripted pass through the sanctioned projection path, landed as its own commit so the
   noise does not bury a real change.
2. Consider collapsing render_markdown_with_extras and frontmatter::render_frontmatter onto one
   serializer. Today they disagree about the trailing newline, which is precisely how this
   diverged.

CLAIM A — no defect. The literal lives at crates/forgeplan-core/src/health/mod.rs:322 (`Verdict::Healthy => "Project looks healthy."`) and is emitted into `next_actions` only through the gate at crates/forgeplan-core/src/health/mod.rs:1699-1717:

        && blind_spots.is_empty() && orphans.is_empty() && at_risk.is_empty() && stale_count == 0;
    if actions.is_empty() && total > 0 && zero_signals { ...push "Project looks healthy. Continue implementation." }

With orphans=15 and possible_duplicates=6 that branch is unreachable. This is the PROB-029 / PROB-063 fix; regression tests pin it at crates/forgeplan-core/tests/health_verdict_test.rs:103-109 and :194-200, plus unit asserts at health/mod.rs:2198, :2234, :2268. GitHub #276 ("forgeplan health returns contradictory verdict and next_actions") is CLOSED. Claim A is a stale report of an already-fixed bug.

(Residual, NOT reproduced, worth noting only: `zero_signals` omits `phase_read_errors` and `stale_ready_drafts`, which DO promote the verdict at health/mod.rs:1198-1199 and :1214-1215, and `generate_next_actions` (health/mod.rs:1623-1632) does not take them. A workspace with only those two signals non-zero could in principle print both lines. Not the reported situation and not observed here.)

CLAIM B — real gap, expected behaviour of the derived index, wrong recovery command used.
1. No read-path reconciliation exists. crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/health.rs:71 calls `common::open_store()`, which at crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/common.rs:11-21 does nothing but `LanceStore::open(&ws)` — no file scan, no lazy sync. `health_report_with_phase` then counts store rows only. So health reports the index, never the filesystem, by construction.
2. The refresh step exists and is `forgeplan reindex` — crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/reindex.rs walks `workspace::ARTIFACT_DIRS`, parses frontmatter, and upserts anything missing (the `None => // Artifact in file but not in LanceDB — create it` branch, reindex.rs:129-175). ADR-016/ADR-017/PROB-076..078/EVID-139..147 all carry valid `id:`/`kind:`/`status:` frontmatter, so that branch would create them. .github/workflows/forgeplan-health.yml:29-47 runs exactly `./target/debug/forgeplan reindex` before `health --ci`, with a comment stating why.
3. The operator's inference that "this is not a stale index, scan-import was run" is wrong because scan-import cannot touch these files. crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/discovery.rs:33-40:
       let skip_dirs = [".forgeplan", "node_modules", ".git", "target", "vendor", ".venv"];
   `forgeplan scan-import` is the brownfield doc-importer; it hard-excludes `.forgeplan/`. Running it can never re-import artifacts that already live there ("9 imported, 0 failed" was importing docs/, not artifacts).
4. ADR-013 is a separate, non-index cause: the file has no YAML frontmatter at all (`head -1` = `# ADR-013: CI Security Gate Policy — PR Trigger vs Push-Only Timing`, status recorded as prose `**Status:** Accepted`). reindex.rs:74-81 skips it with "no id in frontmatter". Even a correct reindex will not surface ADR-013.

ADJACENT REAL DEFECT (docs, not health): every user-facing doc names the wrong rebuild command. docs/README.md:102 ("forgeplan scan-import  # rebuild LanceDB index from markdown") and :110 (fresh-clone recipe `init -y` -> `scan-import` -> "should see all artifacts"), docs/README.ru.md:100 and :108, docs/README.md:125 ("...may cause drift with the LanceDB index until `scan-import` runs"), docs/operations/QUALITY-GATES.md:160 and :450, and CLAUDE.md:31, :545, :666, :671, :673. This is a genuine, code-verified documentation defect and is the proximate cause of the misuse.
why_not_misuse:
I cannot argue this away from operator error, and I am not going to try — the evidence points at misuse, so that is the verdict.

Claim A is simply not reproducible on 0.33.0: a single `forgeplan health` run emits one verdict line, and the code path that would emit the second is provably gated shut with 15 orphans present. It reports a bug closed as #276.

Claim B's numbers are real, but "health disagrees with the filesystem" is the documented contract of a derived index (ADR-003: markdown is source of truth, LanceDB is derived). Nothing in the code prevents it from recovering ADR-016/ADR-017 and the 13 EVIDs.

The one thing that is NOT operator error is why the operator concluded "this is not a stale index": the docs told them to run `forgeplan scan-import`, and scan-import hard-excludes `.forgeplan/` (discovery.rs:33-40), so it silently did nothing for artifacts and reported success on unrelated docs/ files. root_cause:
Three code paths in crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/, all still present at v0.33.0 tip.

(1) PRIMARY — non-idempotent id resolution for placeholder ids
crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/import.rs:539-567 `resolve_artifact_id`
crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/import.rs:572-589 `is_safe_artifact_id`

    if let Some(ref id) = detection.suggested_id {
        let normalized = id.to_uppercase();
        if is_safe_artifact_id(&normalized) { return normalized; }
    }
    // Otherwise, generate next available ID for this kind
    for n in 1..=999 { let candidate = format!("{}-{:03}", kind_prefix, n);
        match store.get_artifact(&candidate).await { Ok(None) => return candidate, ... } }

`is_safe_artifact_id` accepts only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, so the literal `DM-{{auto}}`
declared in the template frontmatter fails the check. Control silently falls
through to the "next free sequential id" loop. Run 1 → DM-001; run 2 → DM-001 is
taken → DM-002; run N → DM-N. There is no content-hash/source-path dedup and no
warning emitted (`ScanImportEntry.warnings` stays empty on this path), so the
report shows a plain green `+` as if a new document had been discovered.

The intended invariant is asserted elsewhere in the same file:
crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/import.rs:974-1014
`scan_import_body_survives_second_import_roundtrip` — "running scan-import twice
on the same file yields Skipped (not duplicate)". That test uses a well-formed
`id: ADR-010`, so it never exercises the placeholder branch. Idempotency is the
declared contract; this is a coverage hole, not a design choice.

(2) WHY THE FILES ARE REACHED AT ALL
crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/discovery.rs:15-26 — SCAN_DIRS includes "docs",
recursed to depth 20 with skip_dirs = [.forgeplan, node_modules, .git, target,
vendor, .venv]. Nothing excludes `*.template.md` / `_TEMPLATE.md` / a `templates/`
subdirectory (`grep -rn '\.template\|_TEMPLATE\|is_template' crates/.../scan/`
returns zero exclusion logic).

crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/detect.rs:44-68 — the PROB-047 mitigation
`is_doc_path` (detect.rs:80-118) is checked AFTER Tier 1 and Tier 2 and only
suppresses Tier 3. Template files declare `kind: glossary` etc., so Tier 1 wins
and the docs/ guard never runs. That precedence is deliberate and tested
(detect.rs:486-506 `path_aware_honors_explicit_frontmatter_under_docs`), so
Tier-1 authority is BY DESIGN — but "kind is authoritative" does not imply
"an id that is a literal `{{auto}}` placeholder should be silently rewritten".

(3) SECONDARY — Tier-2 filename prefix without digits collapses to <KIND>-001
crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/detect.rs:167-188 `detect_from_filename`
crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/detect.rs:192-205 `extract_id_from_name`

    if *prefix == "REF-" && (after.is_empty() || !after.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit()))
        { continue; }        // <-- guard applied to REF- ONLY
    ...
    if num_end > 0 { format!("{}-{}", kind_prefix, num_str) }
    else { format!("{}-001", kind_prefix) }     // <-- silent default

The "require digits after the prefix" guard exists for exactly one of the eleven

resolves to EPIC-001 / SPEC-001 / PRD-001 / ADR-001 and collides with the
workspace's real first artifact of that kind (R3 above).
